label: Reasons versus directed standing: symmetric authority test for issue 1508
summary: Complete unreviewed proposed outcome in docs/notes/natural-goodness-function-and-authority.md, section Reasons and standing. Baseline f9df3e2f7caf5fca6b31a465cbff5e655fedc394. Reused typed certificate and registered Darwall argument; no new theorem. Agent reasons alone do not specify a claimant; a richer realist rights norm can include that content, so no selective burden follows simply from requesting divine jurisdiction. Compared three-layer realist, natural-goodness and authorial accounts with explicit reason, priority, patient-right, representation and jurisdiction commitments. Fixed gratuitous-injury test adds competence, nonconsent, feasible harmless abstention and absence of rescue explicitly; claimant substitution preserves reason while testing who is owed compliance. Strongest rival: basic patient-directed rights with warranted representation and no lawgiver. No accepted-floor conflict found. Rejected free normative assignment, reward requirement, standing from manufacture and primitive-as-false shortcuts. Attribution deferred; no metaphysical winner or root discharge. Draft 1572 f70dab043 is a read dependency only, retaining its conditional entailment and OPEN explanation/application boundaries.
